item.title: Himeji Yukata Festival: The Season's First Summer Robes — Guide
item.description: The Himeji Yukata Festival, held over three nights each June, is one of the oldest and largest summer events in western Japan and traditionally the first occasion of the year for wearing a yukata. It began in the eighteenth century, when a newly arrived lord dedicated a shrine and, so the story goes, told townspeople who had no formal dress to come in their light cotton robes instead. Today several hundred thousand people fill the streets below Himeji Castle over three evenings, among hundreds of food stalls, shrine rites and lantern-lit lanes.

item.title: Chagu-Chagu Umakko: Iwate's Decorated Horse Parade — Guide
item.description: One of Japan’s most colourful festivals — on the second Saturday of June, over 100 horses decorated with elaborate lacquerwork, embroidery and bells parade some 15 km from Onkoshi Shrine in Takizawa to Morioka Hachimangu Shrine. The gentle ‘chagu-chagu’ ringing of the horses' bells gives the festival its onomatopoeic name. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Takizawa → Morioka, Iwate Hours 2nd Saturday of June (morning–afternoon) Admission Free Time needed 2–3 hours Best time Second Saturday of June Highlights 100+ decorated horses in lacquer, embroidery and bells.

item.title: Yosakoi Soran Festival Guide: Dates, Where to Watch & Access
item.description: Every June, Sapporo explodes with colour, music and motion for the Yosakoi Soran Festival — one of Japan’s most exhilarating dance events. Hundreds of teams, tens of thousands of dancers in bold costumes, surge through the streets and across stages, naruko clappers in hand, to powerful remixes of Hokkaido’s traditional “Soran Bushi” fishing song. Born only in 1992, the festival fuses Kochi’s yosakoi dance with Hokkaido’s sea-shanty heritage into a thrilling, modern spectacle that fills Odori Park and the city for several days.
